Krakdhûmvror (I02)

Survey-table region: Serpentspine.

In brief: Guard the western Serpentspine's last Ice-Steel hold, and rebuild northern Dwarven craft and statehood amid the rivalries of five clans.

Narrative: High | Mission-tree length: Long (68 missions available to I02, shared with the I24 continuation) | Mission-tree update context: current scripts support EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Downtime: Medium-high (stagnation, clan politics and a long recovery) | Early pressure: Medium-high | Expansion: Above average, after repairing the foundations

The lone hold in 1444

Unlike most Dwarven holds that must be reclaimed by an adventurer band, Krakdhûmvror is explicitly assigned ownership and a core on province 4208 in the local 1444 start file. Its country history records Quartz Dwarf culture, Ancestor Worship, a republic, the Clan Council and Garlin's accession in 1442. It is therefore a northern remnant state playable directly from 1444. The Dwarven-adventurer formation decision also retains an entry point for I02, but that does not erase its starting holdings: players do not need to treat “first find a home with an adventurer band” as the standard prerequisite. [Local history script] [Local script]

The offline Wiki traces the hold from a fortress built to resist Frost Giants, through a gathering place for imperial exiles, to a Quartz Dwarf society that values skill over bloodline. After the orcish invasions and the collapse of western routes, it survived through Ice-Steel craft, mountain passes and prolonged defence. Those ancient dates belong to Wiki world history; they are not missions already completed by the player in 1444. Krakdhûmvror is not prosperous at the start: local history gives it a long period of reform stagnation, while flavour text says supply trade was nearly cut off after the Greentide. [Wiki] [Local history script] [Local flavour text]

Reform the council before rebuilding the hold

Five ancient clans rotate control of the council, turning a system that once selected people for ability into an exchange among kin groups. The early missions call for restoring the hold, building roads and reconnecting with the surface, then curbing privileges and redistributing land and offices. An older official development diary presented this as a political crisis that could lead either to a free council or to rule by a single clan. The current scripts do include a council, estates and events, but not every reward proposed in a historical diary is automatically a value implemented today. [Local script] [Official development diary]

That is what gives Krakdhûmvror more character than a conventional “Dwarven reconquest.” Political reform is not merely an idea-group bonus: who enters the hold's centres of power determines whether it lives up to its claim that “skill comes before blood.” Ice-Steel training even proposes trials in cold endurance, martial skill and tactics open to everyone from peasants to the monarch, to identify promising officers earlier. You need to stop internal institutions from holding back development before you can push north and through the western Serpentspine. [Local flavour text]

Long survival inside the hold does not mean its institutions are healthy. The defensive tradition lets Ice-Smiths and clans control scarce techniques, and gives them reasons to keep outsiders from gaining office; isolation becomes even harder to change after trade is cut off. Reopening routes to the surface, restoring production and widening the pool of officers are therefore different parts of the same reform. An older official development diary described alternative political outcomes. Treat it as a clue to the theme, not as a promise that every alternative value in the diary is present in the current version. [Local flavour text] [Official development diary]

Ice-Steel, roads and the frozen north

The Ice-Smith estate turns northern survival into a body of craft: Ice-Steel defences, cold-iron engineering, dedicated workshops and later experiments with unusual materials. Related missions ask you to control strategic locations, build roads and upgrade production facilities; the idea of combining a volcanic forge with ice-forging even carries the flavour of a dangerous experiment. Krakdhûmvror's magic is not a wizard's button detached from the economy, but icecraft in service of hold construction, weapons and expeditions. Some missions reach toward northern passes, the Gray King threat and other Dwarven holds. Those are futures the player must pursue, not the borders of an empire already held at the start. [Local script] [Local flavour text]

The current mission file contains 68 missions available to both I02 and I24; it is not “68 exclusive I02 missions, plus another 68 for I24.” A later route to Dwarven unification inherits part of the campaign, so the same missions should not be counted twice. [Local script]

The appeal of ice-forging also lies in its risks. Flavour text presents Ice-Smith workshops and Ice-Mithril experiments as technologies that might run out of control, not cost-free upgrades. Better equipment, expanded hold production and border security all compete for resources. If you enjoy repairing a home first and then retaking routes through technological advantage, that progression is rewarding. If you want the industrial scale of a unified Serpentspine from the opening, Krakdhûmvror's long prerequisites can feel deliberately slow. The missions' far horizons toward other Dwarven holds are future campaign objectives; in 1444, this remains a lone northern hold that must be defended and rebuilt. [Local script] [Local flavour text]

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 67/100 | Authority 52/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 78/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 90/100) | Pluralism 62/100. Alternative route profiles: Free Council (Authority 30) versus single-clan rule (Authority 82).

The v2.1 value classification is Good (69/100), with a stable trajectory. Repairing the hold, building roads, craft training and open officer selection provide public benefits; clan monopoly and dangerous experiments are counterweights. Neither republican government nor expansion through the western Serpentspine determines the moral classification. Public hold works, roads and open officer selection are positive evidence; clan monopoly, military hegemony and dangerous forging experiments limit the assessment. Do not award goodness automatically for being a republic or deduct it automatically for expansion. Recommended for players who enjoy Dwarven holds, factional reform, ice-magic craft and a long revival; not for players who dislike early stagnation, political crises and material prerequisites.

A 2026 campaign report discusses the Ice-Smiths, civil war among the five clans and the long effort to conquer the western Serpentspine; another player comment praises the northern passages and swamp restoration. These are experiences from particular saves, not evidence for current mission counts or formation requirements. See the evidence page for the detailed boundaries. [Community opinion]

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Krakdhûmvror (I02) — Quartz Ideas

Set ID: I02_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
            tag = I02
    }

Quartz Traditions

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • Possible advisors: +2 (advisor_pool; raw value 2).

1. The Chain Bond

Krakdhûmvror is an ancient hold founded by the exiles and criminals of the Dwarven Empire. It has stood alone for centuries against many enemies, fighting near constantly to keep those who would destroy them at bay. This state of perpetual war gave rise to a unique culture amongst the dwarven holds, where sacrifice and skill were valued above bloodline, and the good of the hold was held above that of empire.

The outcasts of the empire gave more for the survival of their hold than any other dwarf in the Empire, be that by gold or blood. This attitude became known as 'The Chain Bond' amongst the people of Krakdhûmvror, a chain between each member of the hold from generation to generation forged in the frozen hardship of the north.

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • National unrest: -1 (global_unrest; raw value -1).

2. 'Zaru ubr Bloth'

'Skill over Blood,' or 'Zaru ubr Bloth,' has long been something of an unofficial motto of the Quartz administration. As it was founded by exiles and criminals, Krakdhûmvror had very few strong clans in its early days. Instead of positions being determined by bloodlines or clans, Krakdhûmvror favors those with individual talent, which has resulted in a far less rigid hierarchy than most other holds. Even those of the most humble of upbringings can rise to the top, and nepotism is all but sacrilegious in the frozen halls of power.

Because of this, Krakdhûmvror has enjoyed an innovative and flexible administration for much of its existence. Many a time a disgraced scion of a royal clan fled to Krakdhûmvror demanding status and position, based on little more than their parentage, and all were told the same thing: 'Zaru ubr Bloth', Skill over Blood.

  • Reform progress growth: +10% (reform_progress_growth; raw value 0.1).

  • Technology cost: -2.5% (technology_cost; raw value -0.025).

3. Orv Zana Architecture

Krakdhûmvror has a reputation of being highly utilitarian in style when compared to the grand marvels of the rest of Dwarovar, and while the halls of the Frozen Hold are not without its grand vistas that could rival those from other holds, this reputation is not entirely unwarranted.

Krakdhûmvror's particular style of architecture, known as "Orv Zana", or "Cold Stone", exists only within the realms of the Quartz Dwarves, and has little pomp and circumstance. This is not without purpose; due to its origin as an expanded fort, every building in Krakdhûmvror is first and foremost dedicated to defence and survival. Even the smallest hovel is built to serve as a fortress unto itself. More than once, these fortifications stalled invading monsters long enough to save Krakdhûmvror from the destruction that befell all other holds in West Serpentspine, leading to a common Quartz Dwarf saying, 'Those in gold houses often end up dead.'

  • Fort defense: +15% (defensiveness; raw value 0.15).

4. Forges of Ice-Steel

Krakdhûmvror is well-known for its unusual type of magic, Icecraft. More akin to Cannorian schools of magic than the runic magic dwarves usually practice, this unique type of cryomancy defies proper classification to any known branch of magic.

The exact details of Icecraft are a closely guarded secret, but it is known that the hold's namesake Frozen Forges channel the biting cold of the northern winds into a magical energy that allows the hold's Ice-Smiths to create Ice-Steel, a versatile metal imbued with the characteristics of ice and freezing water. From weapons that give enemies frostbite and arrows that shatter into shrapnel on impact, to armour that can 'unfreeze' and flow back together, the potential applications of Ice-Steel are widespread.

While the production of the hold's signature steel has over the centuries declined, Ice-Steel armaments are nonetheless common enough that well-off soldiers have at least one weapon or piece of armour made of it, making the Frozenforge Hall's armies a glacial wall of unbending steel and death.

  • shock_damage_received: -15% (shock_damage_received; raw value -0.15).

5. Meritocratic Administration

Krakdhûmvror's meritocratic administration has long been a source of pride for the nation, as unlike in other holds, it rewards talent and ensures that the hold's governing officials are of a higher quality than anywhere else in Dwarovar. Combined with the hold's will to embrace and adapt to changing circumstances, Krakdhûmvror's administration is exceptionally well-placed to deal with situations that would strain the administration of other nations, such as integrating conquered territories into the rest of the country.

  • Core-creation cost: -15% (core_creation; raw value -0.15).

6. Expansion of Midjurdr Kralt

The modern hold of Krakdhûmvror has its roots in Verkal Midjurdr Kralt: Fortress of the World's End. Originally built to protect Dwarovar against the Frost Giants of yore and manned by exiles and criminals banished from the rest of Dwarovar, it became a derelict outpost after the giants' civilisation fell thousands of years ago and was eventually expanded to a hold. As the last outpost of Aul-Dwarov, isolated in the Giants Anvil mountains and disconnected from the Dwarovrod network, the only people who arrived to make a new life for themselves in the hold were those unwanted elsewhere in Dwarovar or those trying to escape their past. This led to the outpost developing a reputation for a solitary culture, and having very little interaction with the outside world.

At least, until the emergence of the orcs. As the holds of Western Serpentspine fell, refugees began to pour to the hold from Amldihr, Orlazam-az-dihr, and Dûr-Vazhatun, desperate for safety from the orcish menace. The rapid expansion of the hold's population forced the dwarves to work with what little resources they had to expand the hold's defences, living quarters, and infrastructure to accommodate a vastly larger population in a relatively short period of time. While this event took place ages ago, the dwarves of the Frozen Hold of Krakdhûmvror still retain the lessons of those days to this day, allowing them to easily integrate foreigners and expand the hold's infrastructure to account for the needs of the people.

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.1).

7. As Unyielding as Quartz

Giant's Anvil is one of the least hospitable environments in all Halann to found an urban society in. The region is undeveloped and isolated from the rest of the world, lacking in resources, and surrounded by hostile monsters.

And yet, the Quartz Dwarves have not only learned to survive in the hostile north, but thrive in it. It takes the most tenacious and determined people to work together in order to survive in as unforgiving an environment as Giant's Anvil, and centuries of hardships and struggle for survival have led to the dwarves of Krakdhûmvror becoming as unyielding as the quartz they get their name from. No matter what they might be up against, the Quartz Dwarves will face the odds with grizzled determination.

  • War exhaustion: -0.03 (war_exhaustion; raw value -0.03).
